terms.grammar: interrogative pronoun: accusative quem, genitive cujus, dative cui, ablative quō; plural quī, quōs, quibus
evidence: Catull. 1.1: cui dōnō lepidum novum libellum?
terms.comment: English “whom” is only the case: quem vīdistī?, whom did you see?; cui?, to whom?; quōcum? (or quīcum?), with whom? Quis homō est? is the stage’s “who’s there?”. Lewis & Short gives quis for the feminine too.

terms.grammar: interrogative pronoun, with nam for emphasis
evidence: Hor. S. 2.7.83: quisnam igitur līber? (Lewis & Short)

phrases.english: Wait, wait. Who’s that over there?

phrases.latin: cui dōnō lepidum novum libellum āridā modo pūmice expolītum?
phrases.english: to whom shall I give my charming new little book, just polished with dry pumice?
whom are you running from, you madman?

phrases.latin: ‘ante’ inquit ‘circumspiciendum est cum quibus edās et bibās quam quid edās et bibās’
phrases.english: “look first,” he says, “at whom you eat and drink with, then at what you eat and drink”
